title: A modified Delphi method to elicit and compare perceptions of industry trends
author: Egfjord, Sund
materials: members of the core business, and (

steps.title: Identify and recruit expert panels
steps.instruction: Select three expert groups (innovation department, core‑business managers, external experts). Aim for 10–15 participants per group (smaller numbers are acceptable for small populations). Invite participants, clearly stating the study format, requirement to take part in multiple rounds, and expected time commitment. Anticipate a 15–25 % dropout after each round and plan invitation timing, response deadlines, and reminder messages accordingly.

substeps.instruction: Define the three expert groups to be compared.
Determine target panel size (10–15 per group).
Send invitation emails describing the study, rounds, and time commitment.

steps.title: Design open‑ended first‑round questionnaire
steps.instruction: Create a questionnaire to be administered separately to each expert group in the first Delphi round. Include a single open‑ended question: “What current and future trends (e.g., social, political, economic, customer behavior, environmental, technological issues etc.) do you expect to have a significant impact on the industry in the future? Name and briefly explain as many trends as you find important.”

steps.title: Clean and consolidate trend responses
steps.instruction: Collect all first‑round responses. Two independent researchers read each response, re‑word unclear formulations while preserving original meaning, split sentences that contain multiple trends, and merge identical trends mentioned by different respondents. Produce one aggregated list of trends for each expert group and have an external colleague independently verify any wording changes.

substeps.instruction: Read each response and note each distinct trend.
Re‑word unclear statements, keeping original wording as much as possible.
Separate multiple trends that appear in a single sentence.
Compile a single list per group.
External colleague checks the re‑worded items.

steps.title: Rate trends using Likert scale
steps.instruction: Present each group's aggregated trend list to the same participants in a random order. Ask each participant to rate every trend on a 1–5 Likert scale (1 = not important, 5 = very important). Ensure anonymity and controlled feedback.

substeps.instruction: Randomize the order of trends for each participant.
Collect individual Likert ratings (1‑5) for every trend.

steps.title: Select high‑importance trends (mean >4)
steps.instruction: Calculate the mean importance score for each trend within each group. Retain only trends whose mean score is greater than 4. Note that the distribution may be non‑normal; the >4 cut‑off defines the set of high‑importance trends.

steps.title: Perform thematic comparison across groups
steps.instruction: Compare the high‑importance trend lists across the three groups. Conduct a thematic analysis to group similar trends that may be worded differently. At least two independent researchers should perform and discuss the analysis, with optional external verification.

substeps.instruction: Group similar wording under common themes.
Discuss and agree on thematic categories.

steps.title: Visualize overlap with Venn diagram
steps.instruction: Create a Venn diagram (or similar visual) showing the overlap of themes/trends among the three expert groups, providing a qualitative illustration of shared and unique perceptions.
